headline: Democrats sweep Congress as oil eases and Canada awaits its budget
summary: The U.S. midterms dominated the week, ending with Democrats projected to win both chambers. Oil swung on Iran talks, Ontario's deficit swelled to a record $16.9 billion, and Canada's federal budget arrives Thursday.

top.headline: Democrats win control of the House and Senate
top.what: Major outlets project Democratic wins in both chambers in Tuesday's midterms, with some races still uncalled.
top.why: It reshapes Washington's agenda, including tariff and trade fights that touch Canada.

top.headline: Oil falls on hopes of an Iran breakthrough
top.what: Brent dropped on deal hopes even after limited U.S. strikes on Iranian sites.
top.why: Oil prices feed directly into Ontario gas and shipping costs.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue as tariffs stay
top.what: Tariffs on Canadian goods remain while talks go on and Democrats talk of repealing them.
top.why: Tariffs affect Ontario manufacturing jobs and prices.

top.headline: Federal budget Thursday to include immigration levels update
top.what: Finance Minister Champagne tables the budget Thursday amid warnings from the budget watchdog that deficits remain deep.
top.why: Taxes, housing and immigration targets affect Ontarians directly.

top.headline: Ontario's deficit swells to $16.9 billion as tariffs delay balanced budget
top.what: Ontario's fall update projects a record $16.9-billion deficit this year and $36 billion over three years.
top.why: In the briefing on 3 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Supreme Court rejects Trump bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots
top.what: The justices quickly refused the administration's emergency request to make California set aside ballots it says may belong to noncitizens.
top.why: In the briefing on 3 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Economy stalls in August, two days after Bank of Canada's hike
top.what: Statistics Canada says the economy was flat in August and probably shrank 0.1% in September, a weak backdrop for the Bank of Canada's first rate increase since 2023.
top.why: In the briefing on 2 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada-wide warrant issued in Bridle Path home invasion
top.what: Toronto police have named a 23-year-old suspect who they say was shot by an accomplice during Thursday's violent home invasion, and two other suspects are still being sought.
top.why: In the briefing on 2 of the last 7 days.
